name_en: Completeness theorem for the real numbers
canonical_name: Completeness of the real numbers (exact order/cut/metric formulation open)
literal_source_claim_en: Completeness of the set of real numbers.
source_attribution: Richard Dedekind / Karl Weierstrass, 1872 (catalog metadata; no work or passage cited)
statement_blocker: The catalog phrase 'completeness of the real-number set' does not select Dedekind/cut or least-upper-bound completeness, metric/Cauchy completeness, or another equivalent formulation. The inspected Dedekind translation states a cut theorem, while pinned mathlib contains both an LUB theorem and a metric-completeness instance. Choosing one without source admission and checked transports would substitute proposition-changing mathematics.
domain_and_universes: Prospective domain is mathlib's Real in Type, but the source must fix whether its relevant structure is the ordered field/cut domain or metric/uniform space and whether any alternate abstract characterization belongs to the root.
conclusion: Prospective family only: the real numbers satisfy one source-selected completeness property. The exact property and conclusion encoding remain open.
degenerate_case_status: No case is excluded before the root is selected. The statement phase must resolve empty and unbounded sets, singleton sets, endpoint ownership, empty cut classes, constant sequences, sequence/filter indexing, uniqueness, and totalized supremum conventions.
candidate_scope_not_credited: every nonempty bounded-above subset of Real has a least upper bound
every nonempty bounded-below subset of Real has a greatest lower bound
every Dedekind separation of Real is produced by a unique boundary real
every Cauchy sequence or filter in Real converges
every bounded monotone real sequence converges
excluded_substitutions: metric completeness substituted for order or cut completeness, or conversely, without a checked source-faithful transport
the Archimedean property, rational density, an irrationality example, or incompleteness of Rat used as the real-completeness root
a greatest-lower-bound, monotone-convergence, or nested-interval consequence used as a selected least-upper-bound root without a checked relationship
mere existence of the totalized sSup operation used without nonemptiness, boundedness, and its IsLUB property
a theorem assuming CompleteSpace Real or ConditionallyCompleteLinearOrder Real used to construct the same intended completeness structure
the Dedekind attribution, catalog year, untrusted verified label, theorem-name match, or intake API probe used as proof credit
